calibration_rulings.title: The title of a lake whose English translates the generic ("Al-Asfar Lake", Arabic «بحيرة الأصفر»).
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar, hubail-lake, delfoon-lake: titles and every mention. Every later lake page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A lake is «جھیل», feminine (plural «جھیلیں»), and in a title it stands BEFORE the name, which is built from the Arabic with its article: «جھیل الاصفر», «جھیل الحبیل», «جھیل الدیلفوون». It is the order of the line for a generic that is an Urdu word («قلعہ العقیر», «مسجد جواثا», «محلہ الکوت») and the reference order. The Arabic generic is never transliterated («بحیرہ» is a sea in Urdu). No gloss of a lake's name where neither source gives its meaning. The press order and its two spellings («الاصفر جھیل», «الاسفر جھیل») go into the entry for search and are not written. Where both sources have the name bare (the head of delfoon-lake's body), it stays bare. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED on two readers for the generic, the order and the gender. THE NAME «الدیلفوون»: both readers failed to read it (the first saw a slip and other words, the second a rendering of 'dolphin'). The rulings that build a name were read again for a lighter spelling and license none: ruling P1 writes a place name as the Arabic writes it, with its article, and drops only the article of a closed list of settled names; ruling P11 touches only the hamza on alif; ruling P17 adds no vowel sign and no gloss for pronunciation. The Arabic «الديلفوون» has two waws and the Urdu has them. The form stays. FOR THE OWNER, as a naming question and not as a pending decision of the line: whether the Arabic spelling with two waws is the intended one, and how the name is said; a form with one waw could only follow a corrected Arabic spelling. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED on three readers for the generic, the order and the gender. The name «الدیلفوون» has failed THREE READERS OF THREE; the form is the Arabic's and stays, and the naming question to the owner stands as round 2 put it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a lake's title begins with the Urdu generic and is equal to its termbase key; verbs and adjectives agree in the feminine.

calibration_rulings.title: The title of a beach ("Al-Uqair Beach", "Salwa Beach"), and the noun for a beach against the noun for a coast.
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-beach and salwa-beach: titles and every mention; salwa-beach::practical[1].value through the title's gender (N87). Every later beach page. ROUND 2: uqair-beach::body, the opening clause (round 2's change 3).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A beach is the compound «ساحل سمندر», masculine, written without an izafat sign; a coast is «ساحل». A title whose English translates everything but a place name takes ruling N43's pattern: the place name as its key, the Urdu possessive, the generic — «العقیر کا ساحل سمندر», «سلویٰ کا ساحل سمندر». It inflects like any phrase («العقیر کے ساحل سمندر پر», «العقیر کا تاریخی ساحل سمندر»). After its first mention the beach may be taken up as «یہ ساحل». AMENDED IN ROUND 2: where the source sets the coast and the beach in ONE CLAUSE, the Gulf's shore is said with «کنارہ» — «خلیج کے کنارے کنارے العقیر کا تاریخی ساحل سمندر پھیلا ہوا ہے» (round 2's change 3) — so that «ساحل» is not said twice in the clause: both readers read that clause twice (first reader, item 20; second reader, item 16). «خلیج کے کنارے» is approved text for the Gulf's shore (al-uqair body, two interface strings) and stands twice more on uqair-beach and once on salwa-beach. A coast named for itself stays «ساحل»: «العقیر کا ساحل» (the area line), «العقیر کے ساحل پر» (faq[3].a), the approved «خلیج کا ساحل» of al-uqair and uqair-castle. What is left of the cost on uqair-beach, charged under compliance: «ساحل» is the coast in the area line and the last answer and the beach in «یہ ساحل». The press forms («العقیر بیچ», «العقیر ساحل») are recorded for search and never written. ROUND 2: the titles and the generic are confirmed on two readers. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. The clause round 2 amended, which two readers had read twice, was read once by the third; the rule for a clause that names both the Gulf's shore and the beach stands as amended. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). No published page carries the leaves of uqair-beach that this entry names; what the entry says of them is the record of the round and binds the page when it is applied, after its own proof pass and blind read. On the published pages this entry is carried by salwa-beach: title, summary, body, and practical[1].value through the title's gender.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the title of a beach is the place name's key, the possessive and the two-word generic; the bare «ساحل» is a coast, or takes up a beach already named on the page. In a clause that also names the beach, the Gulf's shore is said with the word of round 2's change 3, not with «ساحل».

calibration_rulings.title: The title of a place named in honour of a person ("King Abdullah Environmental Park").
calibration_rulings.binds: king-abdullah-park::title. Every later place named after a person (parks, a stadium, a street).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. A place named in honour of a person is a compound with NO possessive after the person's name, every word translated in Urdu order: «شاہ عبد اللہ ماحولیاتی تفریح گاہ», feminine by «تفریح گاہ» (ruling N69). The king's name follows the entry «شاہ عبد العزیز» and ruling N27 («عبد» in two words; the joined form is in the entry for search). A possessive after a person's name says ownership and is not written; ruling N43's possessive is for a PLACE name. Which King Abdullah is not said by the source and is not supplied. The entry stays pending: no Urdu page names this park, and «ماحولیاتی تفریح گاہ» is attested nowhere. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED on two readers. That the noun of ruling N69 is vaguer to a reader than the loan is that ruling's cost and is not reopened; what the park is, the source does not say. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED on three readers for the order and the missing possessive. That none of the three can picture an 'environmental' park is the source's, which explains nothing, and the cost of an unattested compound; charged on the page.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: no possessive stands between a person's name and the generic in such a title.

calibration_rulings.title: The label "Visiting" («الزيارة») on a page that is not a mosque (the row of hubail-lake and delfoon-lake).
calibration_rulings.binds: hubail-lake and delfoon-lake: practical[0].label and value. Every later page that is not a mosque and carries a "Visiting" row.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. On every page that is not a mosque the label of a "Visiting" row is «سیر», ruling N17's word for visiting applied to a label; the mosque label «زیارت» is never reused because the English is the same string. The value of the two lake pages is one string, «کھلا عوامی قدرتی مقام، کوئی فیس نہیں», word for word its English ("natural" kept, no "entry" added). C («داخلہ») is not taken: it changes the source's label to fit one value. B («سیر کے لیے») is on record. FOR THE OWNER (source defect): a label that says what the row is about — the row is the fee and the access. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED. Two readers say the label does not tell what the row holds; nor does the English label. For the owner, as before. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. Three readers of three say the label does not tell what the row holds; nor does the English 'Visiting'. Candidate C, which the third reader wrote unprompted, is on record for the owner with the source defect.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the label of a "Visiting" row is the mosque word on a mosque page only (ruling VISITING-ROW) and the word of ruling N17 for visiting elsewhere; the two lake rows are byte-identical.

calibration_rulings.title: "Open 24 hours" on salwa-beach: which of ruling N65's two strings.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: the masculine string of ruling N65, «24 گھنٹے کھلا رہتا ہے», byte for byte the pair of the translation memory, because the entry of the page's own title («سلویٰ کا ساحل سمندر») is masculine by its head noun. When the batch is applied the pair is entered with the note 'masculine title': ruling N65 observes that a pair of the translation memory names its gender only where someone writes it in `note` (it does not itself ask for the note; proof pass on round 1, finding 21). The feminine string is still exercised by no page; the first park page with this value takes it. ROUND 2: confirmed on two readers. ROUND 3: confirmed on three readers.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the value is one of ruling N65's two strings byte for byte, chosen by the gender of the title's entry.

calibration_rulings.title: "North of Al-Ahsa" («شمال الأحساء») on the two lake pages: a part of Al-Ahsa, or a direction from it?
calibration_rulings.binds: hubail-lake: summary, body, area, faq[1].a; delfoon-lake: body, area, faq[1].a — unchanged from stage 4.
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE WORDING, ruled for the text until the owner answers: B, «الاحساء کے شمال میں», in the seven leaves. Of the three candidates it asserts least: it is the line's approved build for a direction named after Al-Ahsa («الاحساء کے مشرق میں») and, like the Arabic, is also said of a place in a region's north; A states that the lakes are a part of Al-Ahsa and C that they are outside it, and neither source establishes either. Ruling N74 is not reopened: its ground was thulaim's own text. THE FACT is the OWNER'S DECISION and is not settled here: do Al-Hubail Lake and Delfoon lie inside Al-Ahsa (then «الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں» in all seven leaves, one replacement, and the English may say "in the north of Al-Ahsa"), or north of it? With it goes the wider defect: the site uses "Al-Ahsa" for the oasis, the city area and the governorate from page to page. ROUND 2: unchanged; the seven leaves carry one wording and the fact is still the owner's. ROUND 3: unchanged; the fact is still the owner's. RECORDED HERE, in the ruling itself (proof pass on round 2, finding 15): the same Arabic words, «شمال الأحساء», are «الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں» on the applied thulaim, where ruling N74 read them by that page's own text, and «الاحساء کے شمال میں» on the two lake pages; the owner's answer evens the two out. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN. The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 5): N88: do the two lakes lie inside Al-Ahsa?
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the seven leaves carry one wording of the position; none says "part".

calibration_rulings.title: A sentence that names two elements of the page it stands on (asfar faq[1].a: "use the “Open in Google Maps” button in the Visit information card").
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar::faq[1].a (round 2's change 0). Every later answer that sends the reader to an element of the page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B since round 2, and ONE MORE PLACE for quotation marks, beside those of ruling N16, point 5, and of rulings N40 and N72: the label of a button, a link or a section of the page itself, quoted exactly as the Urdu interface shows it, without its arrow or icon, each label in its own pair of marks. The section is «… والے حصے میں». The element is named with the loan the line has already admitted, «لنک» (termbase entry; ruling P16-test), and the verb is «کھولیں», honorific: «“سیاحوں کے لیے معلومات” والے حصے میں “گوگل میپس پر دیکھیں” کا لنک کھولیں۔» (round 2's change 0). Round 1 had «… کو دبائیں» with no noun: both readers understood it and both said one does not 'press' a link on a phone (first reader, item 18; second reader, item 14; both minor); their own verbs are loans with no entry and are not written. The loan for 'button' stays refused (P16-test): the element is a link that leaves the site, and the English 'button' is said as what the element is. The source's semicolon is a full stop (ruling N33). If the interface string changes, the quotation changes with it. Round 1 called this 'a fourth place'; rulings N40 and N72 of the termbase had each counted a place before it (proof pass on round 1, finding 4), so no count is given here. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. The wording of round 2 passed the one reader who has read it. If the interface round rewords the heading the third reader remarks on, the quotation in asfar's answer changes with it, as this ruling already says.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a quoted interface label is byte for byte the ur value of its key in src/i18n/ui.ts without its arrow; the build has no check that ties the two, and the coordinator is told so.

calibration_rulings.title: Three loan-free forms under the owner's rule on loans (P16) and its test (P16-test): four-wheel drive, caravan, booking.
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar::practical[1].value (round 1's change 3). uqair-beach::practical[0].label, practical[0].value, faq[0].q, faq[0].a (round 1's changes 6, 7, 9 and 10), until the owner decides item N100-caravan-loan-or-description. uqair-beach::practical[0].value and faq[0].a for the booking verb (unchanged since stage 1). Every later page that names a four-wheel-drive vehicle or a booking.
calibration_rulings.ruling: The test of ruling P16-test applied to each form, condition by condition. This is the ONE account of it and replaces what round 1 said in three places in three ways (proof pass on round 1, finding 2). (1) FOUR-WHEEL DRIVE: THE LOAN STANDS — «فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑی», plural «فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑیاں»; the cell is «صرف فور وہیل ڈرائیو گاڑی سے». Condition 1 (the native wording is not what the thing is called, shown by the press): met — the Gulf's Urdu paper writes the loan of exactly such vehicles and no native name was found anywhere; the nine-word description was a coinage of this chain. Condition 2 (a blind reader misled): met — the first reader took the native description for any four-wheeled car, on a guarded fact, graded serious. Condition 3 (a dictionary headword OR solid reference attestation): MET IN ITS SECOND, WEAKER CLAUSE ONLY — there is NO dictionary headword; there are five reference pages, two of them running text, and one press page. The test is therefore met as it was for «براؤزر» in b0-ui ('pending: reference attestation only'), and it is NOT the case that all three conditions are met in full: round 1's change 3 and its reader ruling 14 say so in those words and are to be read with this sentence. CONFIRMED BY THE SECOND READER: he read the cell as four-wheel drive only and repeats it in his own words (his items 12 and 36). FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER, because his own rule (P16) is narrower than the test — a loan enters only with an entry that cites a dictionary headword: this is the one loan of the batch admitted on press and reference attestation WITHOUT a headword, and its entry is pending for that reason. If he will have no loan here, the loan-free cell is «صرف چاروں پہیوں کے زور پر چلنے والی گاڑی سے», which a reader took for any car. What decided is the fact: this is the condition he guards with 'only' (build check C37). The figure-and-letter form '4x4' is not written. (2) CARAVAN: the first native description is WITHDRAWN (it reads as a resident's car) and the second, «گھر نما گاڑی» (feminine, plural «گھر نما گاڑیاں»), STANDS IN THE TEXT. What the vehicle is to be called is no longer ruled here: it is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description, with the evidence of both readers and of the press page read in round 2. No third description is coined. (3) BOOKING: THE NATIVE VERB STAYS — «جگہ آن لائن محفوظ کرائی جاتی ہے». Condition 3 is met for the loan (a dictionary headword). Condition 2 is met in its weak form since round 2: the second reader stopped on «محفوظ کرائی» to work out that it means booking, because the same word is the save button and the reserve on these pages; the first reader understood it at once. Condition 1 is NOT shown: the press page read in round 2 writes the loan, but «محفوظ کرانا» is standard written Urdu for reserving a place, and one page that uses the loan does not show that the native verb is not what the act is called. ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, one line: candidate B, «آن لائن بکنگ ہوتی ہے», the word both readers say. ROUND 3: unchanged in all three parts. (1) The loan for the four-wheel-drive vehicle is CONFIRMED BY TWO READERS OF TWO and stays flagged for the owner for want of a headword. (2) The caravan is item N100. (3) The booking verb stays: three readers of three would say the loan, one understood the native verb at once, one stopped on it, one finds it stiff, and nobody misread it; condition 1 of the test is where round 2 left it. It goes to the owner with the caravan, as one question about one row. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). No published page carries the leaves of uqair-beach that this entry names; what the entry says of them is the record of the round and binds the page when it is applied, after its own proof pass and blind read. On the published pages this entry is carried by asfar::practical[1].value, the four-wheel-drive cell, and by nothing else: the caravan and the booking verb stand on uqair-beach alone.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker (read from this entry by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs): none of «چاروں پہیوں کے زور پر», «فور بائی فور» occurs; «بکنگ» is not an admitted loan; «کیمپر» is not an admitted loan. The withdrawn description of the caravan is a retired key of this entry. For the proofreader, checklist item 9: the admitted loan is the termbase entry for the four-wheel-drive vehicle, which cites P16; on asfar the word for "only" is the first word of the access cell.

calibration_rulings.title: "The Kingdom" where the page never names the country (salwa-beach: "the Kingdom's land gateway to Qatar").
calibration_rulings.binds: salwa-beach::body (change 13 of round 1). Every later page whose sources say "the Kingdom".
calibration_rulings.ruling: B. Where a source says "the Kingdom" and the page has not named the country, the Urdu writes the termbase key «سعودی عرب» at that first mention: «جہاں خشکی کے راستے سعودی عرب کا دروازہ قطر کی طرف کھلتا ہے». It names what both sources mean and adds no fact; the Chinese and Russian lines did the same. After the country has been named on a page, «مملکت» may take it up. A is not an error — the Gulf's Urdu paper writes the bare noun for readers who live there — and is the owner's option, one line, if he wants the source's noun kept. The gateway image is the source's and is kept; the first reader's plain "border crossing" is not written. (Ruling N62, which does not name the country beside the province, is untouched: there the source names no country at all.) ROUND 2: CONFIRMED on the second reader. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED for the country's name, on two readers. THE CLAUSE AROUND IT has now cost all three readers a second look (moderate, minor, moderate) and all three arrived at the crossing: the gateway is the source's image, the door that 'opens by a land route' the Urdu's build of it. It is not a misreading and no wording of it has passed a reader, so it stays in the last round, charged on the page. ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, one line: a plain sentence in place of the image, as the first and third readers wrote it («جہاں سعودی عرب اور قطر کی زمینی سرحد ہے»; «جہاں سے سعودی عرب اور قطر کے درمیان زمینی راستہ گزرتا ہے») — each states a border or a route where the sources say a gateway.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the bare word for the Kingdom does not stand on a page before the country's name.

calibration_rulings.title: "Al-Ahsa governorate" («محافظة الأحساء») in a sentence about administrative dependence (salwa-beach).
calibration_rulings.binds: salwa-beach::body (round 1's change 14, round 2's change 4). Every later sentence that says a place falls under Al-Ahsa administratively.
calibration_rulings.ruling: D, with the subject first since round 2. The Arabic generic is not carried into Urdu where the sentence states the fact without it: «سلویٰ انتظامی طور پر الاحساء کے تحت آتا ہے۔» Round 1's change 14 took the generic out; round 2's change 4 sets the subject first, so that the two bare names no longer touch (proof pass on round 1, finding 1: with the adverb first, the subject and the name after it read on first pass as one name). The adverb and «کے تحت آتا ہے» say that the dependence is administrative. THE RULE THAT DECIDES is the style rule `arabisms` of the termbase — an Arabic word of the source is not carried over where the Urdu reader does not use it: as the name of an administrative unit the word has no dictionary headword (the dictionary's word of that spelling is another word), its reference attestation is thin and partly machine-written, and the first reader read it as another word. Round 1 also called on ruling P16-test; that test is worded for English loans and is not needed here (proof pass, finding 20). Stage 4 asked for two readers; one who misreads the word as another word is enough on a sentence whose fact survives without it. THE SECOND READER did not miss the unit: to him the sentence is office language that repeats what the first sentence implied (minor) — the source's sentence. B is refused (the bracket states an equivalence with a district that neither source gives; the pack rules no gloss); C is a loan with a Pakistani meaning of its own; the first reader's «ضلعے» is B without its bracket. The key «محافظہ الاحساء» is retired from this batch's proposals. WHERE THE FORM IS RECORDED FOR SEARCH: in the note of the entry «سلویٰ کا ساحل سمندر» in `termbase_final` of this file; the coordinator copies that line into the note of the repository's entry «الاحساء» when the batch is applied. COST, counted under accuracy: the source's generic is not rendered, and with it the KIND of unit — that the Al-Ahsa meant here is the governorate and not the oasis; after a first sentence that sets Salwa at Al-Ahsa's far end, the adverb alone carries the difference (proof pass, finding 14). The three earlier lines kept the unit on this field. FOR THE OWNER, one line: the unit restored if he wants it named, «سلویٰ انتظامی طور پر محافظہ الاحساء کے تحت آتا ہے۔». A later page that must NAME the governorate as such (a heading, a list of governorates) raises the word again as its own item with this record. ROUND 3: CONFIRMED. With the subject first nobody read the two names as one; two readers call the sentence office language, which is the source's sentence.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker (read from this entry by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs): «محافظہ» does not occur as a whole word. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the sentence keeps the adverb that says the dependence is administrative.

calibration_rulings.title: "Bodies of water" in the owner's guarded claim on asfar (build check C31: «من أكبر التجمعات المائية»), and "a body of water" of hubail-lake («مسطح مائي»).
calibration_rulings.binds: asfar::summary (change 0 of round 1); hubail-lake::body (change 19 of round 1). The Urdu pattern of build check C31, which the coordinator derives from asfar's summary as it stands after the last round.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B for the claim, E for the lake. Both stand in round 2, each contested by one reader, and this is why. (1) asfar's summary: «خلیجی خطے کے سب سے بڑے آبی اجسام میں سے ایک». The three points build check C31 holds every language to are kept and are what the Urdu pattern is to be derived from: AMONG the largest («میں سے ایک»), BODIES OF WATER («آبی اجسام» — not «جھیل», not «قدرتی»), of the REGION («خلیجی خطے», the Gulf bare: ruling P5). THE TWO READERS SIDE BY SIDE: the first read the earlier wording and pictured a man-made tank behind a dam — a wrong picture of the place, on the owner's guarded claim; the second read «آبی اجسام», understood it as water bodies, and found it a word-for-word, textbook phrase. One wording misleads and the other stumbles; on a guarded claim the one that does not mislead stays. The second reader's own wording, «خلیجی خطے میں پانی کے سب سے بڑے ذخیروں میں سے ایک», is candidate C, the noun that misled the first reader, and is not taken. No third wording is coined: none was found that keeps the three points. ON RECORD FOR THE OWNER, one line each: candidate C as the second reader words it; and 'lakes', the first reader's remedy, which the owner's own guard forbids. (2) hubail-lake's body follows the Arabic's other noun: «پانی کا ایک پھیلاؤ», the phrase asfar's body has for the same Arabic word. The second reader finds that the sentence defines a lake as water and sounds translated, and would drop the predicate; both sources open with it ('Al-Hubail Lake is a body of water …'), and a predicate of the field's source is not dropped for register (ruling P24): his sentence is on record for the owner, «جھیل الحبیل الاحساء کے شمال میں ہے۔». The singular «آبی جسم» is attested and is not taken there. (3) The earlier noun and its plural are withdrawn for a natural or drainage-fed lake: the word is a store of water and is read as a dam's reservoir. For a reservoir it is the right word. calibration_rulings.ruling: D SINCE ROUND 2: «(فوارے کی نمائش غروب آفتاب کے بعد)» (round 2's change 7). A is WITHDRAWN: BOTH readers read its noun as a protest before they read a show (first reader, item 43; second reader, item 42), and round 1 had named the second reader as the test. ITS KNOWN COST: it is also the word for an exhibition (so on the applied baiah: things put on display), and nothing attests it of a fountain — 0 pages, as for every other wording. B, the plural of stage 1, is the withdrawn noun in the form the headlines use for protests. F, the press's «فواروں کا رقص», says a dance and several fountains where the Arabic has shows of ONE fountain. C, the verb, says that the fountain runs: less than a show. The known cost showed, as a first-pass stumble that corrected itself inside the bracket; he was not left with an exhibition. THE CELL STANDS. C, the verb, was weighed as the recorded fallback and is not taken: it says that the fountain runs, less than a show, and no reader has read it — the last round does not replace a wording that was understood by one that is unread. THIS RULING BINDS THE ONE CELL AND NO OTHER (proof pass on round 2, finding 2): what a later page calls a show of lights, water or fireworks is raised by that page as its own item and ruled on its own reader, with this record before it. An approved text is not changed by this entry: a later change of the cell is the owner's or a later round's. FOR THE OWNER, as a decision: the loan. All three readers write it («فوارہ شو», «فوارے کا شو», «فواروں کا شو»), after two native nouns that each cost a reader his first pass; his rule on loans (P16) keeps it out, and no page was obtained that writes it of a fountain (P16-test, condition 1). F stays his other option. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; by the proof pass on round 3, finding 1, accepted in the judge's addendum, it is entered with its open question stated, as N88 and N100 state theirs). calibration_rulings.ruling: B. THE SENTENCE, for running text: «مزید تفصیلات کی معتبر ذرائع سے تصدیق ابھی باقی ہے۔» — the confirmation is the subject, the predicate is the plain «ابھی باقی ہے», 'reliable sources' stays, and nothing is promised: no date, no 'will be added'. Where the source names what is unconfirmed, that follows the closed main clause AFTER A COLON (ruling N33: the colon stands where a clause explains what is before it), never inside the clause: «جھیل کے بارے میں مزید تفصیلات کی معتبر ذرائع سے تصدیق ابھی باقی ہے: یہ کتنی بڑی ہے اور یہاں سیاحوں کے لیے کوئی سہولت ہے یا نہیں۔» (round 2's change 6; round 1 had «، یعنی», after which the second reader lost the connection; inside the clause the first reader lost it). The part «مزید تفصیلات کی معتبر ذرائع سے تصدیق ابھی باقی ہے» is letter for letter the same wherever the English says 'Further details … are pending confirmation from reliable sources'. A is withdrawn: its predicate failed the first reader on register and, with the insertion, on syntax. C is refused. THE REGISTER: both readers call the sentence official, each in another wording of its predicate. What they hear is the source's own 'pending confirmation from reliable sources', and how the site states a reservation of its own is not the translation's to change (ruling P25). FOR THE OWNER, one line each, both dropping 'reliable sources': E and F above, the two readers' own sentences. THE SOURCE'S and logged: the Arabic bodies have no such sentence; on delfoon-lake it names nothing. ROUND 3: B STANDS, colon and all, and this is the record it stands on. The two unconfirmed things have been read in three places by three readers — inside the clause, after «یعنی», after a colon — and each reader lost them where he met them; the predicate is office language to all three in both its wordings. No form has passed a reader, so there is none to return to, and a fourth is not tried in the last round. What all three hear is the source's own 'pending confirmation from reliable sources'. THE OWNER'S DECISION, no longer a mere option, because three readers of three wrote the same kind of sentence in its place: E, F and G above each say that the site has not been able to confirm, and each drops 'reliable sources' (G and F also 'further details'). How the site states a reservation of its own is his (ruling P25); if he takes one, it is one sentence on hubail-lake and its short twin on delfoon-lake, with a proof pass and a reading of both. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN (the judge file gives this entry the status "ruled"; by the proof pass on round 3, finding 1, accepted in the judge's addendum, it is entered with its open question stated, as N88 and N100 state theirs). The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 2): N99, the two lakes: the reservation in plain words. Three readers each wrote their own sentence, which says the site has not been able to confirm and drops 'reliable sources'; the sentence in the text keeps the source's wording and cost each of them a reading.

calibration_rulings.title: What is a caravan called on /ur/ — the vehicle one lives in, Arabic «عربات الكرفان», a loan in the source itself: the native description that stands in the text, or a loan?
calibration_rulings.binds: uqair-beach::practical[0].label, practical[0].value, faq[0].q, faq[0].a — unchanged from round 1 until the owner decides. Every later page that names a caravan.
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE WORDING, ruled for the text until the owner answers: A stands in the four leaves — «گھر نما گاڑیاں» (label), «گھر نما گاڑیوں کے لیے» (value and answer), «گھر نما گاڑی میں» (question). It is the one wording a reader has decoded without being misled, and no third description is coined (round 1's rule, kept). THE NAME is the OWNER'S DECISION, because his rule on loans (P16) is what stands between the page and the word both readers say: does a caravan take the loan «کارواں» on /ur/? If yes: B in the four leaves, with its noun where the bare word could be read as a party of travellers — label «کارواں گاڑیاں», «کارواں گاڑیوں کے لیے», «کارواں گاڑی میں» — a termbase entry that cites P16 and says, as the four-wheel-drive entry does, that it rests on press and reference attestation without a headword in this sense; and a proof pass and a blind read of the four leaves. If no: A stays as it is, with its cost on record (a reader is stopped by the label and says nobody calls the thing so). THE JUDGE'S RECOMMENDATION, for what it is worth to him: B — the source itself writes the loan, two readers of two name it unprompted, and the paper his readers read writes it. ROUND 3: unchanged — A stands in the four leaves and the name is the owner's decision. The recommendation is firmer by one reader: B. With it goes the booking verb of the same row (item N90), which all three readers would say with the loan. If he admits either, the leaves of uqair-beach that change need their own proof pass and blind read. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13) AS AN OWNER DECISION, OPEN. The wording ruled above is what the text carries until the owner answers; no leaf waits on the answer. THE QUESTION, as the list for the owner in the judge file words it (its note FOR THE OWNER, decision 1): N100, uqair-beach: does a caravan take the loan «کارواں» on /ur/? Three readers of three write it; «گھر نما گاڑی» stops each reader and is decoded from its row. With it, the same row's verb for booking: all three would say the loan (N90). ‖ THE JUDGE'S ADDENDUM to round 3 (section 6), after a fourth reader: stopped and decoded by three readers of three; «کارواں» written by three readers of four, the fourth writes two other loans. ‖ ENTERED ON APPLY (2026-10-13): uqair-beach is HELD out of the release of batch b6 (the judge's addendum to round 3 corrects the page's score to 89, below the threshold of 90; the name of the caravan is the owner's decision, item N100-caravan-loan-or-description). No published page carries the leaves of uqair-beach that this entry names; what the entry says of them is the record of the round and binds the page when it is applied, after its own proof pass and blind read. No published page carries a wording of this entry.
